title: Multipage app v2 - reloading a page generates websocket connection error on Windows
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Select the basketball page and press reload page button (google chrome browser), generates web socket connection error continuously.

I believe this is a serious bug and deserves a higher priority. We cannot prevent users from pressing that reload button.

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/22366935/07d0358e-102c-419d-844d-04236732a31d)

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/22366935/78ba2c72-e6de-4546-9ee5-02d23383309f)


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
"""
streamlit==1.36.0
"""


import streamlit as st


def Home():
    st.header('Home')


def Basketball():
    st.header('Basketball')


pg = st.navigation(
    [
        st.Page(Home),
        st.Page(Basketball)
    ]
)
pg.run()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code, select basketball page and press the reload button of the browser.

### Expected Behavior

_No response_

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.36.0
- Python version: 3.11.7
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Google chrome


### Additional Information

https://<redacted-host>/t/launched-multi-page-apps-improved-api-and-new-navigation-ui-features/65679/31

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@reporter I'll take a look on this. It seems to be tied to Windows specifically.

@participant1 the 404s are currently expected behavior, but perhaps we can look to simplify. When someone navigates to the page, we assume the host config/connection is on that url, if it fails, we move up a url path directory (and assume we are on a page, and need to the main URL. We should probably look into a solution that would always make the first call work (or provide the correct URL) on load.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I also see this websocket error in my windows dev environment. The error does not occur after deploying to an on premise linux server that we have in the company where I work.

I tried checking the streamlit DEBUG logs but there is no feedback from the log after reloading the page, it's as if the connection wasn't even registred by the framework.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Hey @reporter and @participant4! I was able to reproduce the issue and I figured out the problem. We identify the websocket connection by attempting to connect on the root url first. We fail a test detecting an incorrect connection because of the file separator syntax (what I thought was URL syntax is actually a file syntax). I should have a fix and I can post a wheel file to test this out before merging.

Really appreciate your help in diagnosing!

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Hey @reporter and @participant4 mind trying out this wheel file and verify this works correctly for you.

## To Install

1. Download the following ZIP file. [streamlit-1.36.0-py2.py3-none-any.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15993941/streamlit-1.36.0-py2.py3-none-any.zip)
2. Rename the extension from `.zip` to `.whl`
3. install with `pip install streamlit-1.36.0-py2.py3-none-any.whl`

I might recommend uninstalling streamlit (`pip uninstall streamlit`) beforehand to avoid any conflict.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Hey @participant5 The demo is actually expected behavior. When you refresh the page, session state is cleared, which indicates to return back to the login screen where the st.navigation call does not provide the page you navigated to directly. Therefore, the page is not found. We are working on features that may help store local information on the browser so this context is not lost when you do a refresh like this.
